messages:
support_jim: Heads up — we're getting a spike in 503s for hosted inference since the canary rolled at ~12:00 UTC. Several customers opened tickets complaining timeouts and billing anomalies. sample ticket: https://redwood/support/tkt/1442
monitor-bot: ALERT: api-gateway-prod 503-rate > 5% over 5m (12:03 UTC). Destinations: /v1/generate, /v1/chat.stream. Canary release: canary-2026-03-08-1200 (10%).
alice_oncall: Oncall here — pausing rollouts and triaging. @carol_infra can you freeze traffic/pause canary? Also need the canary config diff.
deploy-bot: Deploy log: canary-2026-03-08-1200 applied by ci-pipeline. Flags: `payload_throttle=true`, `short_kv_cache=false`, canary=10%.
ben_runtime: Noting `payload_throttle` was introduced to limit per-request token fanout for long prompts. It unintentionally flips request routing to legacy gateway path that doesn't honor streaming / retry guards — we've seen it return 503s under burst. Suspect flag is routing some requests to fallback service that is overloaded.
carol_infra: I can cut canary traffic now. running: `orchctl rollout pause canary-2026-03-08-1200 --env=prod`
alice_oncall: Do that + open rollback if pause doesn't bring rates down in 2 mins. Also need repro: can someone get a sample failing request id?
support_jim: Attached a request id from a customer: `req_0a3f4b2c` — logs show upstream `gateway: 503: connection reset` + `kvcache miss` around the same time.
ben_runtime: Reproduced locally with the flag enabled: large multipart prompts + `payload_throttle=true` -> routed to older proxy, hits a path with outdated conv buffer size and returns 503 under load. Workaround: set `payload_throttle=false` or pin to non-legacy route.
carol_infra: Pause complete. Observing metrics: 503 rate dropped slightly from 7.2% -> 4.6% in 30s. Still high.
alice_oncall: Okay, initiate canary rollback to previous tag. Command: ```
orchctl rollout undo canary-2026-03-08-1200 --to=stable-2026-03-07-2300 --env=prod
```
deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by alice_oncall. Starting canary undo.
monitor-bot: NOTE: Rolling window will take ~2m to reflect full change.
carol_infra: Rolling back completed at 12:07 UTC. Confirmed canary traffic removed.
monitor-bot: ALERT RESOLVED: api-gateway-prod 503-rate back to 0.8% (12:09 UTC). Latency returning to baseline.
sara_support_lead: Good job. Support team will reply to affected customers with ETA + apology and credit offer. Please add a short postmortem and root cause writeup. Any immediate follow-ups?
ben_runtime: Short-term: revert `payload_throttle` flag default to `false` in prod, and add a safe-guard so that legacy-route fallback is disabled for canary until we've validated buffer compatibility. Long-term: add integration test for large multipart prompts + routing, and add telemetry on route-fallback counts.
alice_oncall: Assigned postmortem to ben_runtime + carol_infra. We'll track in #incidents-postmortem doc. Also notify billing: `billing@redwood` for any credits.
support_jim: I'll send templated replies and start triage notes for each ticket; attaching repro steps so SRE/devs can follow up.
carol_infra: Follow-up ops tasks: 1) add canary guard to block `payload_throttle` flips without runtime compatibility check, 2) run a controlled load test for `payload_throttle` on staging.
ben_runtime: I'll push a quick hotfix: disable flag default and add route-compat check before enabling in canary. Queueing PR.
alice_oncall: Thanks all. Reaction: :thumbsup: Please avoid further rollouts until we sign off. Postmortem due EOD tomorrow.
sara_support_lead: Closing customer-facing loop now. Will post update once credits applied.
monitor-bot: NOTE: No further 5xx spikes for 20m.
alice_oncall: Keeping thread open for postmortem edits, but incident is effectively resolved.
